llm.summary: This is a disclosed UnifAPI connector skill whose main caution is optional setup guidance that asks users to run an unverified remote installer.

dimensions.detail: The declared runtime authority is Bash(oo *), which is proportionate for a connector wrapper that inspects schemas and runs named UnifAPI actions through oo.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: First-time setup includes curl-to-shell and PowerShell remote installer examples for the oo CLI; this is disclosed and only a fallback after command-not-found, but users should prefer verified installation instructions.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The description covers any UnifAPI request and the action list is large, including social, SEO, rendering, and screenshot operations, but that breadth is disclosed and remains within the stated UnifAPI integration purpose.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill does not install background workers or persistence itself, but first-time login and provider connection steps may create persistent OOMOL authentication or account connections if the user chooses to complete setup.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The artifact coherently routes UnifAPI work through the OOMOL oo CLI and limits normal skill execution to the unifapi connector; credentials are described as handled server-side rather than exposed to the agent.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you intend to use OOMOL and UnifAPI from your agent. Review the oo CLI installation method before running remote installer commands, and pay attention to prompts for any write-tagged action because those may use your connected account or credits.
llm.findings:
[SC2] expected: The remote installer command is present in setup guidance for obtaining the required oo CLI, not hidden runtime behavior; it remains a supply-chain caution because it lacks inline verification.
[SQP-1] expected: The broad invocation language matches a general-purpose UnifAPI connector, and the artifact instructs agents to inspect live schemas and confirm tagged state-changing actions.
[SDI-4] unexpected: Several query-like actions are tagged as write despite the safety text defining write as state-changing; this appears conservative because it would add confirmation rather than silently permit mutation, but the publisher should clarify the labels.
